note: Adapted from Constantino's (1995) revision, originally in English. The soldier and the worker are described; the alate is recorded in the original as unknown (Imago. Unknown.). Soldier measurements: 4 colonies, 4 soldiers, head length 5.20—5.50 mm, maximum head width 4.80—5.10 mm, head height without postmentum 2.80—3.00 mm, frontal tube length 0.06—0.25 mm, left mandible length 2.80—3.00 mm, curvature 0.95—1.15 mm, left mandible M1—M2 distance 0.62—0.69 mm, left mandible width from 0.76 mm. OCR word breaks such as “2.SO-3.00” have been corrected from the context.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Soldier characterized by elongated mandibles, relatively small mandibular teeth, a distinctly inflated postmentum, slender thoracic spines and sparse head pilosity; the most similar soldiers are S. peruanus (shorter frontal tube, more hairs on the vertex) and S. molestus (shorter mandibles, right mandible M1 more prominent, postmentum less inflated, and the head usually with some fine long hairs).

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head capsule short, length and width nearly equal; the sides converging anteriorly; posterior margin of the head nearly round. Frontal tube moderately projecting, the opening not visible in dorsal view, often situated in a small depression. Labrum short, length and width nearly equal; lateral corners of the labrum obtuse; median lobe of the labrum elongated. Antennal segment count as in the measurements paragraph.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Worker: head capsule very large relative to the soldier (compared with this ratio in the other species of the genus); head surface with many scattered setae; postclypeus with about 10 setae. Fontanelle large and round. Antennae 20-segmented. Thoracic tergite spines moderately developed. Mandibles very similar to those of S. spinosus.
